info.name: Automation Exercise - API Testing (10 Tests)
info.description: 10 documented API scenarios for Automation Exercise. Set environment variables before running API007. Uses responseCode in JSON for documented application-level outcomes and HTTP status for unsupported-method cases.

exec: pm.test('HTTP status is 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response is valid JSON', function () { pm.response.to.be.json; });
const data = pm.response.json();
pm.test('Application responseCode is 200', function () { pm.expect(data.responseCode).to.eql(200); });
pm.test('Products array exists and is not empty', function () { pm.expect(data.products).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; });

pm.test('First product has expected fields', function () { const p = data.products[0]; pm.expect(p).to.have.property('id'); pm.expect(p).to.have.property('name'); pm.expect(p).to.have.property('price'); pm.expect(p).to.have.property('brand'); });

request.description: Positive test: retrieve the product catalogue.
Negative test: POST is not supported by the productsList endpoint.

exec: pm.test('HTTP status is 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response is valid JSON', function () { pm.response.to.be.json; });
const data = pm.response.json();
pm.test('Application responseCode is 200', function () { pm.expect(data.responseCode).to.eql(200); });

request.description: Positive test: search products using form-urlencoded search_product=top.

exec: pm.test('Response is valid JSON', function () { pm.response.to.be.json; });
